name: HTTP Behavior
description: Probes a random non-existent URL to verify the site returns a real 404/410 (not a soft 404), verifies the current page returns HTTP 200 to a plain fetch, and checks that no X-Robots-Tag response header contains noindex or none. Agents rely on status codes and headers to know whether a fetch succeeded and whether content may be used.
inputs: HTTP GET of a random probe URL: <origin>/aeo-checker-404-probe-<8 random base36 chars> (2500 ms timeout, redirects followed)
HTTP GET of the current page (shared AnalysisContext page response, 3000 ms timeout, redirects followed)
HTTP response header X-Robots-Tag of the current page

scoring.summary: Three independent criteria, 1 point each. Probe: +1 if the final status is 404 or 410, or if the probe was inconclusive (status 0, 403, 429, 503, timeout, or any status >= 500); 0 if 200 (soft 404) or any other status (e.g. 401, 400). Page: +1 if the final status is 200 or the fetch was unreachable (0, 403, 429, 503, timeout); 0 otherwise (e.g. 404, 500, 502, 401). Header: +1 unless X-Robots-Tag matches /\b(noindex|none)\b/i. A noindex header forces status fail regardless of score.

rules.condition: probe inconclusive: status 0 (network/timeout), 403, 429, 503, timedOut, or status >= 500
probe final status 200 (including a redirect of unknown URLs to the homepage or any 200 page)
rules.message: Unknown URLs return HTTP 200 (soft 404), so agents cannot tell a missing page from a real one
Unknown URLs return HTTP <status> instead of 404

rules.note: Adds an informational issue 'likely bot protection' when status is not 200

rules.message: This page returns HTTP <status> to a plain fetch

rules.condition: page X-Robots-Tag header (case-insensitive name) present and matches /\b(noindex|none)\b/i

scoring.status_mapping: If X-Robots-Tag blocks: fail (score can still be 2). Else score 3 pass, 2 warning, 0-1 fail.
scoring.inconclusive: isUnreachable (status 0, 403, 429, 503 or timeout) on the probe or page still awards that criterion's point; the probe additionally treats any 5xx as inconclusive. No details.inconclusive flag is set and there is no half-weight warning; an unreachable site can score 3/3 pass.

detect.source_procedure: Infer the host's behavior from repo config; mark as 'predicted' since the real answer needs a live server. 1) 404 handling: look for a custom 404 page and whether the host serves it with status 404: static/Vite: 404.html in public/ or output root (Netlify, Cloudflare Pages, GitHub Pages, Vercel static all serve 404.html with 404); Astro: src/pages/404.astro; Hugo: layouts/404.html; Eleventy: 404.html/404.md permalink; Next.js: app/not-found.tsx or pages/404.tsx (Next returns 404 by default). Then look for SPA catch-alls that turn unknown URLs into 200: Netlify/Cloudflare _redirects '/* /index.html 200', netlify.toml [[redirects]] from='/*' to='/index.html' status=200, vercel.json rewrites {source:'/(.*)', destination:'/index.html'}, Cloudflare Pages projects WITHOUT a 404.html (Pages then serves index.html as SPA fallback with 200), Firebase hosting rewrites '**', Next.js catch-all routes app/[...slug]/page.tsx that never call notFound(). Also catch-all redirects of unknown paths to '/' (301/302 to a 200 page = soft 404). 2) Page status: check the audited route exists as a page/file and is not redirected or behind auth (middleware.ts, _redirects, vercel.json redirects, netlify.toml redirects, basic-auth headers). 3) X-Robots-Tag: grep _headers (Netlify/Cloudflare Pages), netlify.toml [[headers]], vercel.json headers, next.config.js headers(), Next.js middleware setting X-Robots-Tag, Hugo/server configs (nginx.conf, .htaccess Header set X-Robots-Tag) for values matching /\b(noindex|none)\b/i on paths covering production pages. Note that Vercel adds 'X-Robots-Tag: noindex' automatically on preview deployments only, not production.
detect.llm_criteria: Judge from the repo's hosting target and framework defaults whether (a) a request for a random nonexistent path would return 404/410 or 200 (SPA fallback, catch-all rewrite, redirect to home), (b) the audited page returns 200, and (c) any header rule applying to production pages sets X-Robots-Tag containing noindex or none as a whole word. Award points exactly as the rules say. If the host cannot be identified, report the probe criterion as unknown rather than guessing.

parity.note: The extension observes live HTTP responses; the repo only lets us predict them. Host defaults (Cloudflare Pages SPA fallback when no 404.html exists, framework adapters, CDN or WAF rules, origin servers not in the repo), dashboard-configured headers/redirects, and edge middleware can all differ from what the source shows. The extension also awards points for WAF blocks and timeouts, which source analysis cannot reproduce.

fix_summary: Add a real 404 page (public/404.html, src/pages/404.astro, layouts/404.html, app/not-found.tsx) and remove SPA catch-all 200 rewrites or redirect-to-home rules for unknown paths in _redirects, netlify.toml or vercel.json (or make the catch-all route call notFound()). Remove X-Robots-Tag noindex/none rules for production paths from _headers, netlify.toml [[headers]], vercel.json headers or next.config.js headers(). Host dashboard settings may still need manual changes.
